newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX electricity seen sharply higher on SW heat.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX electricity seen sharply higher on SW heat.

text.p: NYMEX electricity futures were called to open sharply higher Thursday after setting new life-of-contracts on climbing physical power prices and a rise in natural gas futures values.
"It's just skyrocketing," said a West Coast electricity dealer.

In over-the-counter business, June California-Oregon Border (COB) were quoted at $19.25-19.50 a megawatt hour (MWh) against Wednesday's settlement of $18.10, and June Palo Verde (PV) at $25.50-25.75 versus yesterday's close at $24.15.
"It's just the weather, weather, weather," said a New York futures broker, referring to above-100 degree F temperatures called in the interior section of the Southwest through the weekend.
Limited spot supply due to ongoing plant outages and limited offers from Bonneville Power Administration is expected to lift next-day power prices, market sources said.
Market sources said the power complex would post new highs even if natural gas prices soften.
NYMEX June Henry Hub natgas futures opened 0.6 cent at $2.270 per million British thermal units.
In the Northwest, temperatures are expected to average six to 12 degrees F above normal through Saturday and drop to one to five degrees below normal Sunday.
In the Southwest, readings would run six to 12 degrees F above normal, while coastal areas would remain one to five degrees F above normal.
